column1: # client-go source evidence for Campaign 13 synchronous replica-read policy.

column5: The bounded synchronous selector receives one query-owned deterministic seed and legal peer roles. Global client knobs, labels, load, slow score, busy threshold, NextGen, and async policy remain external.
Leader, follower, mixed, prefer-leader, stale, and learner modes map to explicit synchronous access paths and request flags. TiFlash, proxy, label, load, and async access modes remain external.
The existing API-v1 region lookup boundary remains the sole topology input for replica selection. Keyspace-v2 scans, split RPCs, and broader codecs remain external.

One RegionCache owns ordered peers, exact leader state, shared store generations, request seed binding, and synchronous selector recovery without promoting a successful follower as leader. TTL, buckets, background refresh, production concurrency, and broad batch loading remain external.

The synchronous selector builds legal leader, follower, mixed, prefer-leader, stale, and learner paths; rotates one query seed; handles known-leader and DataIsNotReady transitions; and excludes unreachable peers. Async API, proxy, flashback, labels, load, slow score, and busy policy remain unclaimed.
Exact completed RPC duration remains available to the selector, but slow-score windows and avoidance policy are not promoted by Campaign 13.

The existing sorted region authority continues to provide half-open lookup and stale-overlap protection to replica selection. B-tree concurrency, TTL traversal, batch ascent, and benchmarks remain external.

Replica selection consults the one canonical store generation and excludes unreachable peers without copying store state. Health scoring, labels, load, TLS probes, background refresh, and production concurrency remain external.
